rounds.text: Craftroot Retail Ltd trades at an astonishingly low P/E ratio of just 1.55x based on filed statements [E1], which collapses further to 1.12x against a sector benchmark of 25.22x [E5]. This extreme statistical cheapness is underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 0.09x, where the stock price of ₹ 1.00 sits dramatically below its book value of ₹ 11.1 [E2], compared to a sector benchmark of 3.58x [E6]. Beyond mere asset backing, the business rewards patient equity holders with a tangible 5.00% dividend yield [E4]. Operating performance demonstrates accelerating momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 214% [E19] alongside 3-year and 5-year profit compounding rates of 94% [E18] and 26% [E17] respectively, complemented by a 39% year-on-year sales increase [E55]. Furthermore, the company delivers a positive return on assets of 0.96% that handily outclasses the sector benchmark of -8.52% [E7]. Conceded: [E8], [E12], [E16], [E21], [E22], [E24], [E59].

Craftroot Retail Ltd presents deep structural profitability concerns that heavily discount its apparently cheap headline multiples, anchored by a 10-year compounded profit growth rate of -6% [E16]. This long-term contraction is compounded by a dismal 10-year median return on equity of just 4% [E21], demonstrating that the business has chronically struggled to generate meaningful returns on shareholder capital over an extended horizon. Although short-term metrics appear vibrant, the fundamental earning power remains weak, as evidenced by a current ROE of only 6% [E12] that falls drastically short of the sector benchmark of 29.6% [E8]. Furthermore, the company's median ROE over the last year sits at an underwhelming 6% [E24], proving that recent performance improvements have failed to elevate the firm to industry-standard profitability. Conceded: [E19].

The bear relies heavily on the 10-year compounded profit growth rate of -6% [E16] to claim structural decline, but ignores the dramatic acceleration in the company's recent trajectory, which shows compounded profit growth surging to 26% over 5 years [E17], 94% over 3 years [E18], and an explosive 214% over the trailing twelve months [E19]. Furthermore, while the bear cites a long-term median ROE of 4% [E21], it overlooks the clear upward trend where the median ROE expanded to 9% over 5 years [E22] and reached 15% over 3 years [E23]. Conceded: the 10-year median ROE is 4% [E21] and the current ROE of 6.1% [E12] trails the sector benchmark of 29.6% [E8]. However, the bear's dismissal of short-term metrics ignores powerful operational momentum, including a sales increase of 39% YoY [E55] and strong sales growth [E56]. This exceptional recent earnings velocity is paired with an outstanding dividend yield of 5.00% [E4], providing immediate cash returns to shareholders while trading at an absurdly low P/E of 1.55 [E1] and price-to-book of 0.09 [E2], representing a massive disconnect from the sector benchmarks of 25.22x P/E [E5] and 3.58x P/B [E6].

Conceded: the company displays recent compounded profit growth of 26% over 5 years [E17], 94% over 3 years [E18], and 214% over the trailing twelve months [E19], alongside a 39% YoY sales increase [E55] and strong sales growth [E56]. However, this short-term acceleration emerges against a stark backdrop of a 10-year compounded profit growth of -6% [E16], proving that long-term structural value destruction outweighs fleeting momentum. Conceded: the median ROE reached 15% over 3 years [E23], but the bull ignores that the median return on equity over 10 years sits at a meager 4% [E21], with the current ROE falling back to 6.1% [E12] (or 6% per key ratios [E8, E59]), drastically underperforming the sector benchmark of 29.6% [E8]. Furthermore, while the bull touts the 5.00% dividend yield [E4] and ultra-low valuation multiples of 1.55x P/E [E1] and 0.09x P/B [E2], these optical bargains exist for a micro-cap with a market capitalisation of just ₹ 0.34 Cr [E3] that is suffering from a weak 10-year median ROE [E21] and negative long-term profit growth [E16].
